findings.problem: At the judged revision the `mpd` namespace was still registered by the TUI package with SCHEMA DEFAULTS as its base (no `base` argument at all), so both front doors display defaults while `<workspace>/.mpd/mpd.jsonc` may carry different values — the captain's measured user-visible hazard: a user with hashline.maxDiffChars: 9999 in the file can open /settings, see 20000, and 'correct' it by saving the default, OVERWRITING their own file value. This is acceptance items 4-6 of t39 and ruling (a).
findings.requiredFix: Register the namespace from packages/mpd-config-plugin with a base derived from the workspace file (one live root → that root's file; zero → the mount-time root; many → refuse/degrade explicitly). At the time of writing t39 has this code in flight (baseForNamespace() at index.ts:531-536) — it was NOT present at the revision I judged, and it is not yet judgeable.

findings.problem: Claim 1 (read-in) could not be re-derived: the lane's W11/W12 fail reproducibly (two runs, frame hashes stable) reporting the resolved namespace value / L3 user section as `undefined`, while the SAME boot's settings RPC resolves the written value (value.hashline.maxDiffChars=31415, user.hashline.maxDiffChars=31415, revision 1). Two surfaces of one write disagree, so the read-in layer is unproven at these bytes — either the merge surface is broken or the lane's observation surface is wrong, and nobody has said which is authoritative.
findings.requiredFix: Name the authoritative read-back surface, make it agree with the settings RPC, and re-run the lane green on it; if the descriptor surface was the wrong witness, fix the lane (and say so) rather than the code.

findings.problem: The human-facing docs assert the OPPOSITE of the shipped behaviour: 'The /settings section is not bridged to .mpd/mpd.jsonc … a saved edit … does not rewrite .mpd/mpd.jsonc … not a shipped behaviour' (EN lines 110-122; the same claim at README.zh-CN.md:101-109). The bridge ships, so the docs now mislead a user about where their edit goes — and the pair is out of sync with the built UI. t35 disclosed this as item (g), out of its inScope.
findings.requiredFix: Rewrite NOT CLAIMED #2 in BOTH languages in the same commit (the language-policy pair), pointing at the bridge and the restart semantics; the on-screen text is already correct.
